I have farmed this soil in Iringa for more than seventy years, since I was a boy walking behind my father’s hoe. I put cow manure on this plot every season because it is my own land and I want it to stay strong, and last year I bought one bag of fertilizer from the agro-dealer in town which made the maize grow tall, so I will do the same this year. I sow the seed I kept from my own harvest — I do not buy those new seeds from the shop that finish after one season. My sons and grandchildren will do the planting and weeding, but I will pay for six days of hired help from the village boys when the digging is hard and at harvest time, because my back is old now.
